{{Short description|French physicist (1941–2000)}}
'''Dominique Vautherin''' (October 30, 1941, [[Bois-Colombes]] – December 7, 2000, Paris) was a French theoretical physicist, specializing in [[nuclear physics]].<ref name=Brink>{{cite journal | last=Brink | first=David | title=In Memoriam: Dominique Vautherin | journal=Nuclear Physics News | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=11 | issue=1 | year=2001 | issn=1061-9127 | page=38| doi=10.1080/10506890109411559 | bibcode=2001NPNew..11...38B | s2cid=119676483 | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/10506890109411559 | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=Soyeur>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/S0375-9474(01)00808-9 |title=Dominique Vautherin |year=2001 |last1=Soyeur |first1=Madeleine |last2=Brown |first2=Gerald E. |last3=Gal |first3=Avraham |last4=Langanke |first4=Karlheinz |last5=McLerran |first5=Larry |last6=Richter |first6=Achim |last7=Stachel |first7=Johanna |last8=Tanihata |first8=Isao |journal=Nuclear Physics A |volume=690 |issue=4 |pages=331–338 |bibcode=2001NuPhA.690..331S }}</ref>

==Education and career==
Dominique Vautherin studied from 1961 to 1963 at the [[École polytechnique]] and then, beginning in 1964, did research for the [[National Center for Scientific Research]] (CNRS ). From 1969, he worked at the [[Université Paris-Sud]] in Orsay with Marcel Vénéroni (1929–2015)<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Van Giai | first1=Nguyen | last2=Quentin | first2=Philippe | title=In Memoriam: Marcel Vénéroni (1929–2015) | journal=Nuclear Physics News | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=26 | issue=2 | date=2016-04-02 | issn=1061-9127 | doi=10.1080/10619127.2016.1177379 | page=40| bibcode=2016NPNew..26...40V | s2cid=124496645 | doi-access=free }}</ref> on the [[Hartree–Fock method|Hartree–Fock calculations]] for a finite range interaction with saturation in closed-shell nuclei. For this work Vautherin received the degree of Doctor of Science with Vénéroni as supervisor.<ref name=Brink/> Shortly afterward, Vautherin began his collaboration with [[David M. Brink]] on Hartree–Fock calculations with [[Skyrmion|Skyrme interaction]]s for spherical nuclei,<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.5.626 |title=Hartree-Fock Calculations with Skyrme's Interaction. I. Spherical Nuclei |year=1972 |last1=Vautherin |first1=D. |last2=Brink |first2=D. M. |journal=Physical Review C |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=626–647 |bibcode=1972PhRvC...5..626V }}</ref> and such calculations were then extended to deformed nuclei by Vautherin.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.7.296 |title=Hartree-Fock Calculations with Skyrme's Interaction. II. Axially Deformed Nuclei |year=1973 |last1=Vautherin |first1=D. |journal=Physical Review C |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=296–316 |bibcode=1973PhRvC...7..296V }}</ref> Later, with colleagues, he carried out calculations with Skyrme interactions, and such calculations were then extended by Vautherin to deformed kernels. Later, with colleagues, he carried out calculations with Skyrme interactions for [[giant resonance]]s and nuclear fission.<ref name=Brink/>

He was from 1972 to 1974 a visiting scientist at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) with [[John W. Negele]] and for the academic year 1976–1977 at the [[University of California at Berkeley]].<ref name=Brink/> From 1976 to 1991, he was also an [[Academic ranks in France|associate professor (''maître de conférences'')]] at the École polytechnique.<ref name=Soyeur/> For most of his career, he was a professor in the theory division of the Institute of Nuclear Physics at Orsay, and he directed the division from 1991 to 1995.<ref name=Soyeur/> In 1998, he became a professor at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris VI).<ref name=Brink/>

In the 1970s, he worked with John W. Negele on the development of a [[density matrix]] expansion<ref name=Brink/> ([[Local-density approximation|local density approximation, LDA]])<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Yakovkin | first1=I. N. | last2=Dowben | first2=P. A. | title=The problem of the band gap in LDA calculations | journal=Surface Review and Letters | publisher=World Scientific Pub Co Pte Lt | volume=14 | issue=3 | year=2007 | issn=0218-625X | doi=10.1142/s0218625x07009499 | pages=481–487| bibcode=2007SRL....14..481Y }}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Kikuchi, Akihito|title=Simplification of QPLDA: A practical method to the correction for the LDA band gap problem|class=physics.comp-ph |year=2012|eprint=1209.5845 }}</ref> in nuclear structure studies.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevC.5.1472 |title=Density-Matrix Expansion for an Effective Nuclear Hamiltonian |year=1972 |last1=Negele |first1=J. W. |last2=Vautherin |first2=D. |journal=Physical Review C |volume=5 |issue=5 |pages=1472–1493 |bibcode=1972PhRvC...5.1472N }}</ref> The density matrix expansion "linked the Skyrme interaction with more conventional two-body forces."<ref name=Brink/> He worked extensively with Hubert Flocard on mean field methods and with Nicole Vinh Mau on random phase approximation at finite temperature. Later, Dominique Vautherin also studied [[neutron star]] matter (and the transition from nuclear matter to the densities found in neutron stars) in nuclear astrophysics. With Paul Bonche, he studies the equation of [[state of matter]] in [[supernova]] explosions.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0375-9474(81)90049-X |title=A mean-field calculation of the equation of state of supernova matter |year=1981 |last1=Bonche |first1=P. |last2=Vautherin |first2=D. |journal=Nuclear Physics A |volume=372 |issue=3 |pages=496–526 |bibcode=1981NuPhA.372..496B }}</ref> Vautherin studied hot nuclei with Paul Bonche and Shimon Levit.<ref name=Brink/>

Vautherin collaborated with his former doctoral student Cécile Martin,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.theses.fr/fr/032731965#directeurSoutenue | title=Déposition d'énergie par production de paires dans les collisions nucléaires ultrarelativistes |website=theses.rr}}</ref> and with [[Arthur Kerman]] and other colleagues, on solutions of [[Yang-Mills theory]] using variational methods.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.40.1667 |title=Finite-size and dynamical effects in pair production by an external field |year=1989 |last1=Martin |first1=Cécile |last2=Vautherin |first2=D. |journal=Physical Review D |volume=40 |issue=5 |pages=1667–1673 |pmid=10011987 |bibcode=1989PhRvD..40.1667M |s2cid=33800044 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.47.632 |title=φ4model near the critical point: The Gaussian variational approximation |year=1993 |last1=Kerman |first1=Arthur K. |last2=Martin |first2=Cécile |last3=Vautherin |first3=Dominique |journal=Physical Review D |volume=47 |issue=2 |pages=632–639 |pmid=10015617 |bibcode=1993PhRvD..47..632K }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0920-5632(95)00075-K |title=Ground state properties and glueball spectrum in SU(2) Yang-Mills theory using gauge invariant variables |year=1995 |last1=Martin |first1=Cécile |last2=Vautherin |first2=Dominique |journal=Nuclear Physics B - Proceedings Supplements |volume=39 |issue=2–3 |pages=231–234 |arxiv=hep-ph/9401261 |bibcode=1995NuPhS..39..231M |s2cid=16683941 }} [https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9401261 arXiv.org preprint]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.61.116008 |title=Variational calculations with improved energy functionals in gauge theories |year=2000 |last1=Heinemann |first1=C. |last2=Iancu |first2=E. |last3=Martin |first3=C. |last4=Vautherin |first4=D. |journal=Physical Review D |volume=61 |issue=11 |article-number=116008 |arxiv=hep-ph/9911515 |bibcode=2000PhRvD..61k6008H |s2cid=119415350 }}</ref>

He received in 1975 the [[Prix Paul Langevin]], in 1991 the ''Grand Prix Jean Richard'', and in 2000 the [[Gay-Lussac-Humboldt Prize]]. In 1999 he became the chair of the board of directors of the European Centre for Theoretical Studies in Nuclear Physics and Related Areas (ECT*) in [[Trento]], Italy.<ref name=Brink/><ref>{{cite journal | last=Brink | first=David | title=The European Nuclear Theory Centre in Trento | journal=Nuclear Physics News | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=8 | issue=3 | year=1998 | issn=1061-9127 | doi=10.1080/10506899809410872 | pages=8–10| bibcode=1998NPNew...8....8B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Wambach | first1=Jochen | last2=Leonardi | first2=Renzo | title=The 25th Anniversary of ECT∗: Fostering Nuclear Theory in Europe | journal=Nuclear Physics News | publisher=Informa UK Limited | volume=29 | issue=2 | date=2019-04-03 | issn=1061-9127 | doi=10.1080/10619127.2019.1603553 | pages=12–17| bibcode=2019NPNew..29...12W | s2cid=199135791 }}</ref>
